sources.entry: HandBrake - HandBrake is a video transcoder available for Linux, Mac, and Windows.

summary.one_liner: HandBrake is an open-source video transcoder for Linux, Mac, and Windows that converts existing videos into formats playable on phones, tablets, TVs, game consoles, computers, and web browsers.
summary.what_it_does: HandBrake takes videos you already have and re-encodes them into new MP4, MKV, or WebM files. According to the README, it works with most common video files, including footage from consumer and professional cameras, phones and tablets, screen recordings, and DVD and Blu-ray discs. It leverages tools such as FFmpeg, x264, x265, and SVT-AV1 to do the encoding. The README points to the official documentation for downloading, building, installing, and using the app. It also links to community support channels, a code of conduct, a contributing guide, and Transifex-based translations.
use_cases: convert videos for playback on a phone or tablet
transcode camera footage to MP4 or MKV
rip DVD or Blu-ray discs to digital video files
prepare videos for a TV media player or game console
re-encode video to WebM for web browsers
how_to_run: See the official HandBrake Documentation for downloading and installing HandBrake.
To build from source, follow the build instructions in the official documentation.
notable: Cross-platform desktop app for Linux, Mac, and Windows
Outputs MP4, MKV, or WebM files
Built on established encoders including x264, x265, and SVT-AV1
caveats: The README does not list system requirements or detailed platform-specific install steps; it refers to the external documentation.
Licensed under GPL v2, which carries copyleft obligations for derivative works.
keywords: make videos playable on any device
